name: issue_629_comfort_band_arm_through_open_window
description: The routine comfort-band arm (_apply_comfort_band(), all 7 call sites) must never command an active HVAC mode while a monitored window is genuinely open, even on a warm/off day when nat-vent just released ownership (Issue #629)
notes: Occupant impact: on 2026-08-13 the user turned off the whole-house fan at 06:13am. Within
milliseconds, CA's own routine classification cycle silently commanded the thermostat into
'cool' mode -- even though a monitored window had been open continuously since nat-vent
started, and the day's own classification recommended hvac_mode='off'. No pause fired, no
notification, and the log never even mentioned the mode change. The AC then idled through
open windows for over an hour and tripped a comfort_undertemp incident (indoor already
below the heat floor) along the way.
Root cause: _set_temperature() (Issue #301 single-setpoint architecture) always bundles
hvac_mode into every climate.set_temperature call. select_comfort_band()'s two-way
ternary (active = 'floor' if hvac_mode == 'heat' else 'ceiling') treats an 'off'-day
classification the same as a cool day for edge-selection purposes -- by design, for the
'lazy comfort band' safety net (Issue #249) that arms a wide band on ANY day type when
windows are closed. The only thing standing between an open window and this write is
_paused_by_door -- upstream flag bookkeeping that can (and did) fail to engage in time: a
coordinator refresh fired apply_classification() moments after nat-vent released ownership,
before any door-pause reconciliation had a reason to run.
Fix: a structural choke-point guard directly inside _apply_comfort_band() -- the single
write point all 7 comfort-band callers funnel through -- refuses to arm an active mode
while a monitored window is genuinely (debounce-settled) open, and pauses via the existing
_pause_for_door_window() machinery instead. Mirrors the WHF/AC mutex choke-point already
structural inside _set_hvac_mode() (Issue #392 Fix 1b). Exempt while nat-vent/WHF genuinely
owns HVAC (handle_occupancy_away/vacation legitimately arm a wide, inert setback band
while an active nat-vent session continues to own real HVAC behavior -- see
away_natvent_exits_at_comfort_ceiling/away_with_active_natvent_transition).
Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10):
(a) Scenario effectiveness: reverting the choke-point guard in _apply_comfort_band()
makes this scenario fail -- the 06:13:44 classification cycle would command
hvac_mode=cool via set_temperature, exactly reproducing the incident. Verified via
revert-test before promoting.
(b) Docs-production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md's Anchors table gets a new
row for this choke-point, alongside the #620/#623 door-pause entries.
(c) User outcome: a whole-house fan turned off right after nat-vent leaves the AC exactly
where it was (off), instead of silently starting to idle in cool mode through open
windows -- comfort-restore now correctly pauses and notifies instead.

events.note: Early morning: indoor above the heat floor, outdoor cooler -- favorable for free cooling.

Window opens before any classification exists yet (_current_classification is still None, so _is_within_planned_window_period() trivially returns False and does not intercept this dispatch). outdoor 65F < indoor 71F, indoor > comfort_heat 68F -- nat-vent activates, WHF turns on.

Warm-day classification: windows recommended, HVAC off -- matches the real incident's own classification. Nat-vent is already active, so DEFER_NAT_VENT gates this cycle regardless -- no comfort-band arm attempted, matching correct production behavior.
User manually turns the WHF off -- no CA context, on_fan_turned_off() fires, releasing HVAC suppression and starting the fan-off grace (matches the real incident's 06:13:44.097).

A routine classification cycle fires moments later -- exactly the coordinator refresh that raced nat-vent's release in production. Window is still open, and windows_recommended=true means _is_within_planned_window_period() grants its 'don't fight the user' exemption (deliberately, per Issue #51/#53 -- see automation.py's docstring), so _paused_by_door stays False and this cycle reaches _apply_comfort_band() unguarded by the door-pause subsystem. The choke-point guard added in this issue is the only thing that can still catch it.

assertions.reason: Window opens with favorable conditions -- nat-vent activates normally.

Issue #629: the comfort-band arm following the fan-off classification cycle must never command 'cool' (or 'heat') mode through the still-open window -- neither via set_hvac_mode nor via set_temperature's bundled hvac_mode parameter (the actual mechanism that fired in production).

The choke-point guard in _apply_comfort_band() must set _paused_by_door=True when it refuses to arm through the open window, so the pause is visible on the Status card and subsequent cycles correctly stay gated via decide_scheduled_band_gate()'s DEFER_PAUSED, instead of silently no-op'ing.

verdict.summary: The comfort-band arm refuses to command an active HVAC mode through a genuinely open monitored window, even immediately after nat-vent releases ownership (Issue #629)
verdict.observed_behavior: sensor_open -> natural_ventilation -> user turns fan off externally -> routine classification cycle fires -> comfort-band arm is intercepted by the choke-point guard, HVAC stays off, _paused_by_door=True
verdict.expected_behavior: No active HVAC mode is ever commanded (via any code path, including set_temperature's bundled hvac_mode) while a monitored window remains open
